Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN leaders confident of delivering joint manifesto pledges
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional leaders are confident that their joint manifesto for the Melaka election is realistic, achievable and focused on the people's needs.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the manifesto had been carefully drawn up by strategists from both coalitions to ensure its pledges could be fulfilled.
He said PN had appointed four to five strategists to work with their BN counterparts on drafting the manifesto.
"We see this as a targeted manifesto, and we are confident that its pledges are achievable.
"Based on the previous Melaka government's track record, 97 per cent of its earlier manifesto pledges have been fulfilled.
"With the cooperation between BN and PN, we believe our ability to deliver on these commitments will improve further," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the BN-PN manifesto launch at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Takiyuddin said the manifesto covered key areas, including the cost of living, education, housing and other basic needs.
He said its pledges were intended to benefit Melaka's 1.06 million residents across all age groups.
"It covers everyone, from newborns to senior citizens. I believe no major aspect has been overlooked.
"We hope the government will be able to fulfil all the promises outlined in this manifesto," he said.
MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said the manifesto contained practical initiatives that ordinary Malaysians could understand and benefit from.
He said measures such as assistance for communities and newly married couples, as well as efforts to reduce the prices of essential goods, addressed pressing concerns among the people.
"Rather than coming up with big, bombastic figures or grand promises, what matters is whether these pledges can be translated into actual assistance and initiatives that benefit the people.
"We cannot simply distribute money to the people without a proper economic foundation.
"There must be ways to attract investments, generate income and create jobs, including the 20,000 new employment opportunities promised for Melaka," he said.
Wee said the manifesto also outlined plans to strengthen Melaka's economy, including positioning the state as a data centre hub and accelerating economic growth.
He described the proposals as evidence of careful planning by both coalitions.
"I believe this is a well-thought-out plan, particularly in terms of how economic development can support the assistance and initiatives promised to the people," he said.

Title: Bursa directed Zetrix AI to address 2025 dividend non-payment, disclose material information
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia has directed Zetrix AI Bhd to address the non-payment of its 2025 final dividend by Nov 23, and disclose material information by Nov 11, to address several issues.
This includes outstanding remittances to the Road Transport Department (RTD) and payment demands from the RTD and Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
Other concerns include the resignation of all independent directors and external auditors, the issuance of shares under the Employees' Share Option Scheme, and the financial and operational impact of the suspension of Zetrix AI and its subsidiary as collection agents for the RTD.
The regulator said it viewed recent developments at Zetrix AI with serious concern, particularly the non-payment of its 2025 final dividend and the withdrawal of its declared 2026 interim dividend.
Bursa Malaysia said the directives were issued under Paragraph 2.23 of the Main Market Listing Requirements to safeguard investor interests and ensure the timely disclosure of material information.
"Bursa Malaysia takes compliance with its listing requirements seriously. Listed issuers are expected to uphold high standards of corporate governance, transparency and accountability at all times," it said.
The capital market regulator said it must thoroughly examine all relevant facts and circumstances, assess evidence of any potential breach and comply with applicable procedures before taking enforcement action.
Bursa Malaysia reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding market integrity, strengthening corporate governance and transparency, and sustaining investor confidence through a fair and orderly marketplace.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three killed in two separate crashes along North-South Expressway
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: Three people, including a retired policeman and his wife, were killed in two separate accidents along the North-South Expressway (PLUS) near here today.
Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the first accident occurred at 12.16pm when the couple died after their motorcycle was involved in a three-vehicle collision at KM114.4 northbound, near Tikam Batu.
He said the crash was believed to have occurred when a Perodua Bezza carrying a married couple stopped on the emergency lane to change drivers before re-entering the left lane and colliding with two motorcycles.
"The Yamaha XMAX motorcycle ridden by Suhaimi Saidin, 64, with his wife, Normah Hashim, 60, as pillion rider, was thrown into the right lane. Both were pronounced dead at the scene," he said in a statement today.
Hanyan said the rider and pillion rider of the other motorcycle, a Keeway XDV180 EVO, aged 18 and 15 respectively, were seriously injured.
The 36-year-old driver of the Perodua Bezza and his 41-year-old passenger were unhurt.
He said the injured victims were taken to Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital for treatment, while the couple's bodies were sent to the hospital's Forensic Department for post-mortem examinations.
Suhaimi, who retired on Aug 11, 2022, had served at the Service Division of the Penang Police Contingent Headquarters.
In a separate incident at about 9am at KM108 northbound, near the Sungai Petani Selatan exit, a technician was killed when his motorcycle crashed into the rear of a lorry parked on the emergency lane.
Hanyan said investigations found that the lorry, which was travelling from Penang to Sungai Petani, had broken down and stopped on the emergency lane. Its driver had placed a warning triangle behind the vehicle.
"About 10 minutes later, the Honda ADV 160 motorcycle ridden by the victim is believed to have failed to notice the lorry before crashing into its rear," he said.
He said the victim, Mohamad Saifudin Saad, 43, who worked for a company in Penang, suffered head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
The 34-year-old lorry driver was unhurt.
Hanyan said both cases were being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Indonesia presses ahead with equity market reforms after MSCI downgrade warning
Article:
LONDON: Indonesia is accelerating reforms aimed at addressing the equity market concerns that prompted index provider MSCI to threaten its emerging-market status and remove it from indexes tracked by funds, Investment Minister Rosan Roeslani told Reuters.
MSCI froze some index changes over opaque share ownership and suspected coordinated trading, warning in October it could relegate Southeast Asia's largest economy to "standalone market" status, potentially prompting investor outflows.
The MSCI announcement triggered the steepest one-day fall in Indonesian stocks in 28 years.
In an interview with Reuters, Rosan said authorities had made progress on free float and the disclosure of holdings above 1 per cent but more work was needed on enforcement and concentrated stocks.
"We are continuing to improve our capital market, and hopefully we can accelerate this improvement," he said, adding that Indonesian authorities were meeting regularly with MSCI.
"We just try our best, try to work with MSCI, because I know it's the best for all of us," he said.
The government's reform efforts, which were launched before MSCI issued its warning but have since been significantly stepped up, come as Indonesia is also seeking more private investment in state assets through privatisation.
Rosan said the government planned to begin divesting stakes in state-owned entities next year, through IPOs or private placements. Airports, seaports and healthcare, which piqued the most investor interest, are likely to go first, he added.
"We have a choice to do the privatisation on the holding level or the operational level directly, or both," he said, declining to give further details.
"We are very open to find a lot of different structure(s) when we do the privatisation in the coming years."
WEALTH FUND STRATEGY: MORE INVESTMENTS, MORE BOND ISSUES
Rosan, who also heads Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara, said it planned to open offices in New York and Hong Kong.
"There are a lot of investors there, and they are hubs for financial instruments. Also, at the same time, we are looking at operational opportunities," he said.
The fund also plans a Saudi office after buying land and hotels in the Muslim holy city of Mecca to serve Indonesians participating in the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
Rosan said Danantara's planned investments next year could surpass this year's estimated US$14 billion to take advantage of the variety of "under-pressure ... and undervalued" assets, though he declined to name specific opportunities.
He added that he expected that the fund's domestic to international investment ratio — currently a roughly 80 per cent to 20 per cent split — could eventually shift to 60 per cent to 40 per cent.
Danantara could also issue more debt after its debut US$1.5 billion Eurobond in June, if market conditions and yields are favourable, Rosan said. Options include Panda and Dim Sum bonds and a 30-year Eurobond — or a combination.
"We are open to have a 30-year bond also, because there is also the appetite for us, based on the investor feedback ... So we might do it also in the future," he said.

Title: Melaka polls: Najib house arrest issue will not affect PN campaign
Article:
AYER KEROH: The issue surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest will not affect Perikatan Nasional's campaign in the Melaka election.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter concerned Najib's constitutional rights, which must be respected regardless of political affiliation.
He said every Malaysian convicted of an offence had the right to seek a royal pardon under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"Every citizen has rights under the Constitution. This includes the right to seek a pardon from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong after serving a certain period of imprisonment.
"That is his constitutional right, and it must be respected by everyone. It applies to all citizens, not just selected individuals.
"There should be no double standards in the application of the law," he said after attending the joint Barisan Nasional-PN manifesto launch at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Earlier, it was reported that Najib's lawyers had paid the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
The payment paves the way for Najib, 73, who has been held at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
However, a source told the media that Najib had undergone a medical check-up at Kuala Lumpur Hospital and was expected to return to prison after completing it.
Takiyuddin also called on the government, particularly the Home Ministry, to explain why the house arrest arrangement for Najib had yet to be implemented.
He said that once a court-imposed fine had been paid, any prison term imposed in default of payment would no longer apply.
"When a fine has been paid, the question of imprisonment in default of payment no longer arises.
"As such, the period of imprisonment to be served at home should be implemented as soon as possible.
"If this has not been done, we demand an explanation from the government, particularly the Home Ministry, as to why it has yet to be implemented," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cabinet clears move to transfer scheduled waste powers to Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Cabinet has approved an amendment order that paves the way for Sarawak to assume legislative powers over scheduled waste management from the Federal Government.
The Borneo States (Legislative Powers) (Amendment) Order 2026 has been cleared by the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) and will be submitted for the consent of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, had agreed to a memorandum from the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry on the order.
"This decision reflects the commitment of the prime minister and the government to continue strengthening the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), particularly in ensuring that the delegation of federal legislative powers to the Sarawak government can be carried out in an orderly and effective manner, in line with Article 95C of the Federal Constitution," he said in a statement today.
Fahmi said the amendment was an important step towards suspending the enforcement of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 in Sarawak.
This would allow scheduled waste management functions to be transferred to the state government in an orderly manner while avoiding overlapping jurisdiction between the Federal and state governments, he said.
He said the initiative was part of the government's ongoing efforts to fulfil its commitments under MA63, particularly the delegation of federal legislative powers over environmental matters to the Sabah and Sarawak governments.
"The transfer of powers will be carried out in phases, with scheduled waste management as the initial phase," he said.
"The Madani Government remains committed to ensuring that the MA63 implementation agenda is translated into concrete actions and decisions to strengthen Federal-state relations and safeguard the interests of the people of Sabah and Sarawak."
In November 2024, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly
passed the Natural Resources and Environment Bill 2024.
Sarawak Natural Resources and Urban Development Minister II and Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Awang Tengah Ali Hasan had said that full authority over environmental management and pollution control would allow the state to set its own environmental quality goals.

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN unveils cradle-to-grave welfare measures
Article:
AYER KEROH: A range of welfare measures, from savings incentives for newborns to funeral assistance, forms part of the social agenda in the joint Barisan Nasional–Perikatan Nasional election manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today.
The manifesto outlines financial assistance at various stages of life for the state's 1.06 million residents.
"Among the approaches outlined in this manifesto is giving dedicated attention to community welfare across the entire journey of life, from the moment a child is born right through to the twilight of their years," said Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Under the proposals, newborns in the state will receive a one-off deposit into the National Education Savings Scheme (SSPN) from January 2027.
Primary school pupils will receive transport fare assistance to attend Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardhu Ain (KAFA) classes, while secondary school students sitting the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) examinations will be offered free tuition.
For youths entering the workforce, the coalition has pledged one-off technical training grants for those from B40 households pursuing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) qualifications. The initiative is part of its broader plan to create 25,000 job opportunities.
Newly married couples with a combined monthly household income of less than RM3,500 will receive a one-off cash assistance, while senior citizens will continue to receive welfare assistance. The manifesto also includes state-funded funeral assistance.
Ab Rauf said social welfare should cover people throughout their lives, rather than consist of isolated, one-off handouts.
"This approach conveys a distinct principle: that public welfare does not stop at a single station in life, but encompasses the entirety of their life cycle as an absolute commitment touching everyday existence," he said.
"Indeed, the final arrangements before they are called to the Almighty will also be given proper care," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother jailed 5 years for abusing daughter; husband denies 4 rape charges
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A mother was sentenced to five years in prison for abusing her 9-year-old daughter, while her husband pleaded not guilty to four charges of raping the child.
During the proceedings, a video showing the mother abusing the girl, recorded by a complainant, was played in court.
The woman pleaded guilty to causing physical injuries to her daughter at the car park of an apartment building in Penampang between noon and 12.05pm on Oct 22.
She was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, punishable under Section 31(1) of the same Act, which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both, upon conviction.
In mitigation, the unrepresented woman said she had three young children and that her husband had also been arrested.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Shafferah Mad Iskim said the child had been subjected to abuse since she was 7.
She said the medical report confirmed multiple abrasions, bruises and bite marks, while the victim had also been diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
The mother was sentenced to five years' imprisonment, effective from Oct 22, the date of her arrest, and fined RM10,000. In default of payment, she will serve an additional 12 months in prison.
The court also ordered her to enter into a 3-year good behaviour bond of RM2,000 without deposit, with one surety, upon completing her prison sentence.
She was further ordered to perform 120 hours of community service after her release.
The mother, 29, and her husband, 34, appeared separately before Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Her husband, a bakso seller and holder of an IMM13 document, was charged with raping their daughter on four separate occasions in February, April, May and October this year at an apartment in Penampang.
He was charged under Section 376(3) of the Penal Code, which carries a prison sentence of between 8 and 30 years and a minimum of 10 strokes of the cane upon conviction.
The court fixed Dec 11 for pre-trial case management.
Bail was not granted, and the man, who was unrepresented, will remain in custody pending the next court date.

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN pledges 25,000 affordable homes, 25,000 job opportunities
Article:
AYER KEROH: A target of 25,000 affordable homes and 25,000 job opportunities over five years are among the key economic pledges in the joint Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today.
The coalition pledged to build 25,000 affordable homes over the next five years to help first-time buyers secure housing and address affordability concerns.
It also committed to creating 25,000 job opportunities, alongside one-off technical training grants for youths from B40 households pursuing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) certifications.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto sought to balance immediate welfare needs with long-term capacity building by expanding entrepreneurship opportunities and vocational training pathways, enabling local youths to build careers without having to leave the state.
"For young people entering the workforce, we offer 25,000 employment opportunities," he said.
"There are young people seeking jobs to build their future, and young couples dreaming of their first home.
"This is the reality of life that guided us in framing this joint manifesto," he added.
The housing and employment targets are part of a wider manifesto comprising 113 initiatives under six pillars, with the theme "Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara" (Building Melaka's Future, Prospering the Nation).
Of the 113 initiatives, 20 priority commitments have been identified to improve the daily lives of people across Melaka.
Ab Rauf, who is also the caretaker Chief Minister, said the pledges were intended to address people's needs at different stages of life, while ensuring economic growth translated into sustainable livelihood opportunities, support for micro-businesses and higher-skilled jobs for the next generation.

Title: Microlink gets 12 month extension, RM60mil extra for advance passenger screening contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Microlink Solutions Bhd said its wholly-owned subsidiary Microlink System Sdn Bhd has secured a RM59.58 million contract extension from the Home Ministry for the Advance Passenger Screening (APS) system to be used by the Immigration Department, bringing the total contract value to RM137.92 million.
The 12-month extension will run from Nov 6, 2026 to Nov 5, 2027, extending the overall contract period to 36 months from the original 24 months.
"The additional scope under the extension covers continued application services for the onboarding of additional airlines, infrastructure services, software license renewals, and support and maintenance services for the APS system," said Microlink in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The original contract, valued at RM78.34 million, was awarded in November 2024 for the design, development, supply, installation, integration, testing and commissioning of the APS system.
Microlink said a supplementary agreement would be signed with the ministry to formalise the extension. The subsidiary is required to furnish a performance bond in accordance with the terms of the contract, said Microlink.

Title: Melaka polls: Free water, ambulance services among BN-PN pledges
Article:
AYER KEROH: Monthly water subsidies and free ambulance services are among the key pledges in the joint Barisan Nasional–Perikatan Nasional (BN–PN) election manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today.
The coalition pledged free domestic water for households consuming less than 20 cubic metres, or 20,000 litres, a month.
It also promised a free state-wide ambulance service under its '1 PBT 1 Ambulans' model, with each local authority operating dedicated vehicles to reduce the cost of medical transportation for the public.
For parents facing examination-related expenses, the coalition also pledged free tuition classes for all Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) candidates in Melaka.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the pledges were aimed at easing household expenses related to utilities, housing, healthcare and children's education, and providing financial relief to the people.
He said the commitments had been assessed in terms of financial sustainability and administrative feasibility to ensure they could be implemented if the coalition secured a mandate in the state election.
113 initiatives across six pillars
The cost-of-living measures form part of a broader manifesto comprising six pillars and 113 initiatives, including 20 priority commitments aimed at improving people's daily lives.
Titled "Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara" (Building Melaka's Future, Prospering the Nation), the manifesto covers key areas such as affordable housing, education, employment, healthcare and economic infrastructure.
Ab Rauf, who is also the caretaker Chief Minister, said the pledges were not merely a list of figures and programmes, but measures intended to address the needs of people at different stages of life, from young families to senior citizens.
He said the manifesto also outlined plans to prepare the state for future challenges, including rapid technological changes, shifts in workforce demands and broader economic transitions.
The joint manifesto marks a significant development in Melaka's political landscape, with BN and PN campaigning under a shared platform for the first time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies after falling from 22nd floor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A man died after he was believed to have fallen from the 22nd floor of a residential building here this morning.
Johor Baru Selatan district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police received an emergency call about the incident about 7.30am.
He said the victim was found unconscious before an ambulance from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) arrived at the scene.
"An examination by HSA medical personnel confirmed that the victim had died at 8.08am.
"Based on initial investigations and a physical examination of the victim at the scene, no criminal elements have been detected so far," he said in a statement today.
Azrul Hisham said preliminary investigations indicated that the victim had fallen from the building's 22nd floor.
He said the body was sent to the HSA Forensic Unit for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
"The investigation is ongoing, and the public is advised against speculating or spreading unverified information on social media, as this could interfere with investigations and affect the privacy and sensitivities of the victim's family," he said.
Anyone with information about the incident is urged to contact the Sentral police station chief at 07-223 2222 to assist in the investigation.

Title: Ringgit slips against US dollar amid global risk-off sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed lower against the US dollar on Friday, weighed down by a broad risk-off sentiment across global markets amid renewed selling pressure in the semiconductor sector.
At 6pm, the local currency slipped to 4.0565/0610 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0445/0490.
SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit faced pressure as investors turned cautious amid heightened uncertainty in global markets.
"We are also seeing some safe-haven demand for the US dollar against other major currencies such as the euro and Australian dollar, which is spilling over into Asian currencies," he told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit was weaker against the US dollar today by 0.22 per cent compared to RM4.0557 post US midterm elections, with concerns on artificial intelligence investment appearing to dominate the financial markets.
"Traders are also awaiting US nonfarm payrolls data tonight, with consensus estimates putting total job creation at 65,000 in October versus 29,000 in September," he said.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It fell versus the Japanese yen to 2.5616/5646 from 2.5548/5578 at Thursday's close, but it edged up against the euro to 4.5315/5365 from 4.5428/5478 yesterday and strengthened vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.4304/4365 from 5.4455/4516 previously.
The ringgit performed mixed against its Asean peers.
The local currency appreciated versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1657/1694 from the previous close of 3.1679/1717 and gained against the Thai baht to 12.0898/1105 from 12.1013/1199 yesterday.
However, it eased versus the rupiah to 224.2/224.6 from 223.6/224.0 on Thursday and slipped vis-a-vis the Philippine peso to 6.43/6.44 from 6.42/6.43.

Title: Lee Yeow Seng steps down from IOI to focus on IOI Properties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd has announced the resignation of Datuk Lee Yeow Seng as its non-independent non-executive director, effective Nov 6, to focus on his leadership responsibilities at IOI Properties Group Bhd.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, IOI Corp said Lee's resignation would allow him to concentrate on advancing IOI Properties' strategic priorities and creating long-term value for shareholders.
It said the decision also reflects IOI Properties' significant presence in Singapore and Lee's role as executive chairman of IOIPG Malaysia REIT, which is scheduled to be listed on Bursa Malaysia on Nov 25.
Lee, 47, is the brother of IOI Corp group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Chor.
He is also deemed a major shareholder of IOI Corp through his interest in Progressive Holdings Sdn Bhd, with an indirect interest of about 3.13 billion ordinary shares or 49.8 per cent stake.
IOI Corp said Lee had no disagreements with the board and there were no matters arising from his resignation that needed to be brought to shareholders' attention.
Meanwhile, IOI Corp announced the appointment of Datuk Yeo How, 70, as an independent non-executive director, effective today.
Yeo previously served with IOI Group for 25 years, from 1983 to 2008, holding various positions, including chief financial officer and executive director.
During his tenure, he oversaw the group's financial management, mergers and acquisitions, funding strategies, investor relations and governance matters.
He was also involved in expanding IOI Group's downstream businesses, including palm oil refining, oleochemicals and specialty fats.
Following his departure from IOI Group in 2008, Yeo joined Singapore-based Royal Golden Eagle (RGE), where he led the group's agribusiness expansion into midstream and downstream activities.
He was involved in the growth of Apical Group, which became a major integrated palm oil player with operations spanning refining, oleochemicals, functional fats, biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel.
Yeo retired from RGE in September 2026.
He currently serves as lead independent non-executive director of IOI Properties and previously sat on the Malaysian Accounting Standards Board and the board of the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Title: TRC Synergy-CCCC-UFUK Semarak JV lands RM2.69bil Penang LRT works contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TRC Synergy Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary TRC Construction Sdn Bhd (TRC) and its joint venture (JV) comprising China Communications Construction Company Ltd (CCCC) and Ufuk Semarak Sdn Bhd (UFUK) (CCCC-TRC-UFUK JV) secures RM2.69 billion Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) project works contract worth RM2.69 billion.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction company said the contract entails the design, construction, and completion of a sea-crossing viaduct, including spans for navigation channels, an elevated station, and other associated works from Macallum to Penang Sentral.
"The duration of the contract is for five years. It will not have any effect on the issued share capital or the shareholdings of the substantial shareholders of the company.
"Based on TRC's 30 per cent participation interest in the JV, the contract is expected to contribute positively to the revenue and earnings of the company over the duration of the contract," it said.
Yesterday, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) announced the award of the RM2.69 billion Civil Main Contract 2 Package (CMC2) to CCCC-TRC-UFUK for the Penang LRT's cross-sea extension linking Penang Island to the mainland.

Title: Malaysia's flood insurance gap leaves households exposed to billions in losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia suffered close to RM1 billion in flood-related losses in 2024, but a significant proportion of the damage was uninsured, highlighting the country's widening protection gap against natural disasters.
General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM) chief executive officer Chua Kim Soon said many households and vehicle owners remained inadequately insured despite the increasing frequency and impact of extreme weather events.
He said East Malaysia had the lowest flood insurance coverage, with only 21 per cent of fire and motor insurance policies carrying flood extensions.
"This compares with 29 per cent on the east coast and 28 per cent each in the central and northern regions, while the southern region recorded the highest proportion of policies with flood coverage," he said at PIAM's Monsoon Readiness Media Roundtable here today.
Chua said the insurance gap was also evident across Asia, where floods accounted for more than 50 per cent of economic losses caused by natural disasters, estimated at US$31 billion (RM125.816 billion), but only about five per cent of those losses were insured.
He said Malaysia had also recorded RM5 billion in losses from landslides between 1961 and 2023, while about 26,000 storm-related incidents had been reported since 2021, resulting in property damage.
Chua called on homeowners to review their insurance coverage, particularly the distinction between houseowner policies, which protect buildings, and householder policies, which cover household belongings and contents.
He said many homeowners only insured their buildings to meet bank requirements when taking out housing loans, leaving furniture, electrical appliances and other personal belongings exposed to financial losses.
"Most of the insurance policies they have do not cover the contents. They only insure the building," he said, citing the Putra Heights fire as an example of the importance of having adequate protection.
On motor insurance, Chua said only 13 per cent of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles in Malaysia had additional flood coverage, compared with 50 per cent of electric vehicle (EV) owners.
He said EVs recorded an average flood-related loss of RM8,404, significantly lower than the RM34,000 recorded for ICE vehicles.
He attributed the difference partly to EVs' protected electrical systems and high-voltage isolation technology, as well as lower exposure and higher flood insurance uptake among predominantly urban EV owners.
"EVs are less prone to flood damage. Their protected electrical systems and high-voltage isolation technology help reduce flood-related risks," he said.
Meanwhile, Chua said at least 12 insurance policies linked to Malaysians who went missing in the Nepal glacial flash floods had been fully settled, with payments made to their next-of-kin.
He said preliminary records had identified more than 50 insurance policies associated with the incident, although these did not necessarily represent an equivalent number of individuals, as one person could hold multiple policies.
"The policies included travel insurance, annual personal accident insurance and group personal accident coverage.
"We expect more of these matters to be resolved in the coming weeks. We will also continue providing support to the next-of-kin of those missing," he said.
Chua said the insurance industry was working with Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) to reach out to affected families and expedite claims processing.
Some 54 Malaysians went missing following glacial flash floods in Nepal on Aug 26, particularly around the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border area.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MISC leads RM4bil joint bid with EPF, Yinson Legacy to privatise Yinson
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MISC Bhd, together with Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund Board (EPF) had launched a privatisation bid for Yinson Holdings Bhd through a members' scheme of arrangement valued at approximately RM4.03 billion.
Under the proposed scheme, the joint offerors intend to acquire all remaining ordinary shares in Yinson not already owned by the excluded founding and pension fund shareholders at an offer price of RM2.50 per share in cash.
The transaction is being undertaken by a consortium comprising MISC and its indirect wholly owned unit MISC OBU Holdings (L) Pte Ltd (MOHPL), Yinson Legacy and its shareholder and Yinson's group executive chairman Lim Han Weng, EPF's wholly owned vehicle Kwasa Layar Sdn Bhd, and acquisition vehicle MY Offshore Holdings Sdn Bhd (MYOHSB).
As of Oct 23 — the latest practicable date (LPD) — the excluded shareholders, comprising Yinson Legacy, EPF, Lim, and his children, hold a combined direct stake of 44.80 per cent in Yinson. MISC currently holds no direct or indirect interest in the group.
Prior to completion, internal reorganisations will see Lim and his children transfer their individual shareholdings to Yinson Legacy, raising its direct stake to 27.73 per cent, while EPF will transfer its 17.1 per cent stake to Kwasa Layar.
Both Yinson Legacy and Kwasa Layar will subsequently roll their Yinson shares into MYOHSB on a one-for-one basis at an issue price matching the RM2.50 offer price.
Upon completion, MYOHSB will own 100 per cent of Yinson. MISC and Yinson Legacy will each hold an effective 41.5 per cent equity interest in MYOHSB, with Kwasa Layar holding the remaining 17.1 per cent.
MISC's capital commitment for its portion of the scheme is estimated at RM3.03 billion, which the group intends to finance through an indicative mix of 75 per cent bank borrowings and 25 per cent internal cash.
The cash consideration of RM2.50 per share represents a 10.13 per cent premium over Yinson's closing price of RM2.27 on Nov 5, the last full trading day prior to the service of the proposal letter.
It is also at 11.29 per cent to 26.47 per cent premium over Yinson's five-day, one-month, three-month, and six-month volume weighted average market prices (VWAP) leading up to the proposal letter.
The offer price is also at a 16.28 per cent premium over Yinson's closing price of RM2.15 on Aug 28, the trading day preceding the initial announcement of exploratory talks.
Based on Yinson's unaudited results for the period ended July 31, 2026, the offer values the group at an implied enterprise value of RM25.10 billion, representing a trailing twelve-month EV/EBITDA multiple of 8.72 times and an implied price-to-book ratio of 1.36 times.
MISC highlighted that these metrics fall squarely within the valuation ranges of comparable global floating production players, such as Bumi Armada Bhd, BW Offshore Ltd, MODEC Inc, and SBM Offshore NV.
The acquisition provides MISC with an expanded footprint in the global floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) and floating storage and offloading (FSO) sectors. Yinson brings a substantial offshore contracted revenue backlog of approximately US$19.3 billion as of July 31, 2026, securing medium-to-long-term earnings visibility.
Operationally, the union creates substantial scale, as Yinson owns and operates eight FPSOs and three FSO units across Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia, while MISC brings a fleet of six FPSOs, five FSOs, and one semi-submersible floating production system.
MISC's board noted that joining forces enables both groups to share technical and engineering expertise, capture supply-chain efficiencies, and pursue large-scale, capital-intensive offshore projects deconsolidated from MISC's direct balance sheet.
This structure allows MISC to grow its offshore division while preserving capital flexibility for its shipping operations, the group said.
Based on illustrative pro forma effects on MISC's audited FY2025 financials, the group borrowings, excluding lease liabilities, would increase from RM12.21 billion to RM14.49 billion, raising gearing from 0.36 times to 0.43 times.
Its net assets per share would see a slight dip from RM7.62 to RM7.61, the group said.
Incorporating MISC's 41.5 per cent share of Yinson's financial year ended Jan 31, 2026 net profit of RM176.22 million, alongside estimated annual borrowing costs of RM106.79 million and transaction fees, MISC's illustrative enlarged net profit would climb to RM1.73 billion from RM1.70 billion, lifting basic earnings per share from 38.1 sen to 38.8 sen.
Since EPF is a major shareholder in both MISC (15.48 per cent) and Yinson (17.1 per cent), the transaction constitutes a related party transaction for MISC under Bursa Malaysia Listing Requirements.
EPF will abstain from voting at MISC's forthcoming extraordinary general meeting, MISC stated. Public Investment Bank Bhd has been appointed as the independent adviser to non-interested shareholders, while AmInvestment Bank serves as principal adviser. UBS AG Singapore Branch acts as international financial adviser.
The transaction is subject to disinterested shareholder approvals at a court-convened meeting (requiring at least 75 per cent approval by value, with dissenters not exceeding 10 per cent), High Court sanction, and extensive antitrust clearances across jurisdictions including Angola, Brazil, the Economic Community of West African States, Nigeria, Vietnam, and the European Union, alongside approvals from the Petroleum Commission of Ghana and the Norwegian Ministry of Energy.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, the privatization is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027

Title: Melaka polls: BN uses 2021 manifesto record as benchmark for new pledges
Article:
AYER KEROH: Melaka Barisan Nasional has fulfilled 97 per cent of the pledges made in its manifesto for the 2021 state election.
State BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the achievement would serve as a benchmark for the state government in assessing the effectiveness and delivery of its future commitments to the people.
The caretaker Melaka chief minister said the achievement demonstrated the state government's commitment to ensuring that election promises were not merely political pledges but translated into tangible results through transparent and accountable governance.
"For the record, based on a review of our previous manifesto covering the 2021 to 2026 period, we have fulfilled 97 per cent of the pledges made during the last state election.
"This serves as an important benchmark for us to continue evaluating our performance and ensuring that new pledges are implemented transparently and responsibly.
"The manifesto has one clear objective, which is to ensure that Melaka's development translates into tangible benefits that improve the lives of its people," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after launching the joint BN and Perikatan Nasional manifesto for the  Melaka election here.
Meanwhile, Ab Rauf said the manifesto marked the first collaboration between BN and PN, reflecting a joint effort that he hoped would lead to electoral success on Nov 14.
He said both coalitions had held several meetings to exchange views and ideas before reaching a consensus on the pledges presented in the manifesto.
"We held several meetings, exchanged views and ideas, and eventually reached the consensus that we presented earlier.
"This is certainly our first joint manifesto and also marks the beginning of our cooperation.
"We hope this joint effort will translate into a shared victory on Nov 14," he said.

Title: Muhyiddin calls for clarity on rules governing Najib's house arrest
Article:
MELAKA: The government has been urged to clarify the rules governing house arrest for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to ensure the public understands its legal basis and the restrictions imposed.
Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said it remained unclear whether house arrest was governed by specific regulations similar to those imposed on prison inmates.
He said the public should know whether individuals under house arrest were free to do as they pleased or subject to certain restrictions, including limits on their physical movements.
"We have previously issued a statement saying that we did not understand what house arrest meant. Does it follow rules similar to those in prison?
"As far as I remember, there is no specific law governing the regulations for house arrest.
"Are those under house arrest free to do whatever they want, or are they restricted? Are there restrictions, both in terms of physical movement and the manner in which they are detained at home?" he said.
He was speaking after attending a programme to engage with residents at the Sungai Udang state constituency in the Tangga Batu parliamentary constituency here today.
Also present were Bersatu vice-president Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin, secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz and the party's Sungai Udang candidate, Major (Rtd) Abdullah Mahadi.
Najib was reported to have paid the RM50 million fine imposed on him in the SRC International Sdn Bhd fund misappropriation case at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Registry today.
On Sept 18, the former Pekan member of parliament received a conditional pardon from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
Najib, 73, was sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million after being found guilty by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on July 28, 2020, on seven charges relating to the misappropriation of RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.
On Aug 23, 2022, the Federal Court dismissed Najib's final appeal and upheld his conviction and sentence. He began serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison on the same day.
Muhyiddin, who is also a former prime minister, further called on the government, particularly the Home Ministry, to provide a legally grounded explanation of how house arrest would be implemented so that the public could understand the arrangement.
He said that if there was no specific legislation governing house arrest, the government should draft the necessary provisions and table them in Parliament.
"If a specific law is needed, it should be drafted and tabled in Parliament. But for now, I do not know what legal basis or regulations are being used to allow house arrest to be implemented," he said.

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN manifesto outlines 113 initiatives for state
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional  and Perikatan Nasional  have unveiled a joint manifesto for the Melaka election, outlining 113 initiatives to spur development and improve the well-being of the state's people.
Themed "Building Melaka's Future, Prospering the Nation", the manifesto is built around six key pillars and 20 major commitments aimed at addressing the daily needs of the state's 1.06 million people.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh  said the initiatives included free water, 25,000 affordable homes and 25,000 job opportunities over the next five years.
He said the manifesto covered housing, the cost of living, education, employment, public welfare, economic growth and the state's development needs.
"Among the main offers are free water bills for monthly consumption below 20 cubic metres, a target of providing 25,000 affordable homes within five years, free ambulance services and free tuition for Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia candidates.
"These offers address four needs closely linked to people's lives, namely household expenses, housing, access to healthcare services and children's education," he said.
He was speaking at the manifesto launch at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Rauf said the manifesto, introduced under the banners of "BN Sayang Rakyat" and "Muafakat Melaka", was designed to benefit all segments of society, regardless of race or religion.
He said the coalition had adopted a comprehensive welfare approach that addressed people's needs at every stage of life.
"For newborns, we are offering a one-off National Education Savings Scheme (SSPN) contribution beginning Jan 1, 2027.
"For schoolchildren, we are offering transport fare assistance for Kafa pupils, while young people from B40 families will receive one-off assistance to pursue Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) certification programmes.
"For young people entering the workforce, we are offering 25,000 job opportunities.
"Newly married couples with a household income below RM3,500 will also receive a one-off cash gift, while welfare assistance for senior citizens will continue," he said.
Rauf said the manifesto also included assistance with funeral arrangements, reflecting the coalition's commitment to supporting people throughout their lives.
He said the initiatives were intended to balance immediate welfare needs with long-term economic development, particularly through job creation, support for small businesses and the promotion of youth entrepreneurship.
"State development must be viewed from two perspectives — economic progress and the well-being of the people.
"Our objective is to balance today's welfare needs with economic development that can sustain people's livelihoods in the future," he said.
Rauf described the joint manifesto as a significant development in Melaka's political landscape, bringing together two coalitions with different political histories and approaches under a common agenda.
"Two political coalitions, two different histories of struggle, are now standing on one stage to present a shared direction. What unites us today is not merely political interests, but a far greater responsibility towards the people.
"We want every step taken, every plan formulated and every commitment offered to ultimately benefit the people and Melaka's future," he said.
With campaigning entering its sixth day, Rauf said voters were mature enough to distinguish between election promises made merely to attract support and proposals capable of improving their lives.
He said a manifesto should not simply outline what a coalition intended to achieve over five years, but also explain the problems it sought to resolve, the opportunities it aimed to create and the benefits people could expect.
"I believe the people of Melaka are mature enough to assess which promises merely sound appealing and which offers can truly transform their lives.
"When we talk about a manifesto, the question is not only what we want to accomplish in five years.
"We must also answer three important questions: What problems do we want to solve? What opportunities do we want to create? And what benefits can the people expect?" he said.
Rauf stressed that the credibility of any manifesto would ultimately depend on the coalition's ability to deliver its commitments.
He said every initiative must be backed by proper planning, financial assessments, administrative coordination and implementation monitoring.
"No matter how comprehensive a manifesto may be, it must ultimately be judged by its ability to be implemented.
"Every commitment presented must be followed by planning, an assessment of financial capacity, administrative coordination and monitoring of its implementation," he said.
Rauf expressed confidence that cooperation between BN and PN would translate into responsible governance and tangible benefits for the people of Melaka.

Title: Maybank IB allotted 225mil shares in Big Caring IPO for price stabilisation measures
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Investment Bank has announced that it has been granted an over-allotment option comprising up to 225.15 million shares for the upcoming initial public offering (IPO) of Big Caring Group Bhd (BCG).
In a Bursa Malaysia filing by BCG, Maybank IB stated that BCG's shares may be subject to stabilising action following the IPO. The option is designated strictly for the purpose of covering any over-allotments of shares during the IPO.
The maximum threshold represents exactly 12.0 per cent of the total number of shares offered under the IPO.
The stabilisation period will officially commence on Nov 19, the listing date of BCG on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia. According to the announcement, Maybank IB's mandate to stabilise the share price will remain active until the earlier of two specific milestones:
The date falling 30 days from, and including, the official listing date; or
The date when the stabilising manager has successfully purchased the full aggregate limit of 225.15 million shares on the open market.
The mechanism is designed to prevent or slow a decline in the market price of the shares following their debut, providing early market stability for incoming investors.

Title: MARC downgrades YNH's RM700mil sukuk on weak cash flow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has downgraded YNH Property Bhd's RM700 million Sukuk Wakalah programme rating to BIS from BBIS and placed it on MARCWatch Negative, citing weakened liquidity and heightened refinancing and repayment risks.
The rating agency said the downgrade reflects YNH's weak internal cash flow generation, continued reliance on asset disposals to meet financial obligations and limited earnings visibility.
"These pressures are compounded by a shortfall in the sukuk reserve account, which has resulted in a technical default," it said.
As at Oct 27, YNH's reserve account stood at RM54.4 million, RM6.8 million below the required RM61.2 million, resulting in a technical default, the rating agency said.
The company is required to rectify the shortfall within a 30-day remedy period to prevent an event of default.
"While YNH has indicated its intention to remedy the shortfall within the permitted period, the occurrence of the reserve-account shortfall nonetheless underscores the company's constrained liquidity and limited capacity to meet its funding requirements through internally generated cash flows," added MARC.
The rating agency said the MARCWatch Negative placement reflects significant uncertainty over YNH's ability to meet its RM170 million sukuk maturity on Feb 26, 2027.
It said repayment would largely depend on the timely completion of planned asset disposals, with any further delays potentially increasing repayment risks.
YNH's sukuk repayment is substantially dependent on the proposed RM170 million disposal of its Desa Sri Hartamas land to Sunway Living Space Sdn Bhd.
The transaction, first announced in May 2023 and extended several times, is expected to become unconditional by the end of November 2026, with completion targeted for January 2027.
MARC Ratings said the disposal is expected to generate RM105 million in net proceeds after settling approximately RM65 million in outstanding loans tied to the land.
"Given the proximity of the expected disposal completion to the February 2027 sukuk maturity, however, YNH has limited headroom to absorb any further delays in the transaction," it added.
YNH is also disposing of a 1.05 hectares freehold land parcel along Jalan Sultan Ismail in Kuala Lumpur to Chin Hin Property (JSI) Sdn Bhd for RM455 million.
The transaction, expected to be completed by January 2027, comprises RM409.5 million in cash and RM45.5 million in redeemable preference shares in a 70 per cent-owned subsidiary of Chin Hin Group Property Bhd.
The cash proceeds are intended to fully redeem YNH's RM350 million outstanding unrated perpetual bond and settle outstanding coupon obligations.
MARC Ratings said while both disposals could ease liquidity pressures and reduce borrowings, YNH's immediate financial position remains heavily dependent on their timely completion.
Meanwhile, the rating agency said YNH's weak operating performance provided limited support to its liquidity position.
The company's revenue declined to RM106.9 million in the financial year ended 2026, reflecting limited progress billings from ongoing projects.
YNH currently has few active developments, mainly Solasta Dutamas in Kuala Lumpur and a shop lot development in Manjung, Perak.
"The limited development pipeline constrains near-term earnings and operating cash flow generation, reducing YNH's capacity to rebuild liquidity organically," it said.

Title: Genetec exits battery JV with Citaglobal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genetec Technology Bhd is exiting its battery energy storage joint venture (JV) with Citaglobal Bhd, by disposing of its 50 per cent stake in Citaglobal Genetec BESS Sdn Bhd (CG BESS) to its former partner.
The stake, which comprises 250,000 ordinary shares, will be acquired by Citaglobal New Energy Sdn Bhd (Citaglobal NE), a subsidiary of Citaglobal.
The transaction also includes a proposed debt transfer, where Genetec will transfer to Citaglobal NE all rights and interests regarding an intercompany balance of RM2.24 million that is currently owed by CG BESS to Genetec.
The total purchase consideration for both the equity disposal and the debt transfer is a nominal sum of RM1.00.
Genetec's board deemed this valuation fair and reasonable, noting that it was arrived at after considering the full impairment of Genetec's investment in CG BESS, as well as the full impairment of the intercompany balance.
The JV, incorporated in January 2023 to manufacture electricity distribution apparatus and batteries, has incurred losses since the commencement of its operations. As of June 30, CG BESS recorded an unaudited loss after tax of RM51,911.63 and with net liabilities of RM4.35 million.
The rationale for the transaction centers on diverging corporate strategies. The Board stated that Genetec and Citaglobal possess distinct business objectives and strategic priorities, and terminating the collaboration enables each party to pursue its respective direction independently.
Upon the deal's completion, the prior Collaboration Agreement established on Oct 6, 2022, will be terminated.
Genetec said the exit will not materially impact the group's earnings, net assets, share capital, or gearing for the financial year ending June 30, 2027. Barring unforeseen circumstances, the transaction is expected to be finalized by the last quarter of 2026.

Title: Zahid, Turkish higher education council chief discuss stronger TVET cooperation
Article:
ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today received a courtesy call from Turkish Higher Education Council (YOK) president Prof Dr Erol Ozvar.
On the agenda were ways to strengthen cooperation in technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
The 40-minute meeting began at 11.30am and was attended by Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Discussions included the introduction of a modular credit system and greater exchanges of academics and students between the two countries.
Zahid said the meeting was also aimed at reviewing memoranda of understanding (MoUs), cooperation agreements and technical agreements signed between higher education institutions in Malaysia and Turkiye.
"We already have close cooperation between universities in Turkiye and Malaysia. I hope the discussions will help strengthen these ties further.
"Mara institutions, particularly Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia and UniKL, have established good cooperation with several universities here," he told a press conference after the meeting.
He said Mara's 270 TVET institutions, together with other educational institutions, could provide a platform for expanding technical training cooperation.
Zahid said Malaysia also planned to send experts to Turkiye for training-the-trainers programmes while expanding exchanges involving lecturers and students.
He said cooperation could also extend to the defence industry, particularly through joint research involving technical universities and industry players.
Ozvar said the meeting had opened up opportunities to expand cooperation in higher education and scientific research, building on the close ties between universities in both countries.
"We would like to bring our universities together more frequently. Today's agenda included possible areas of collaboration between universities in both countries.
"There are ongoing scientific research projects involving universities from both countries, and we would like university leaders to identify projects in priority areas pursued by Malaysia and Turkiye," he said.
Also present on the Turkish side were the council's ambassador and adviser to the president, Dr Ergun Bekar, and YOK Department of International Relations head Mustafa Efe.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8.

Title: [UPDATED] Najib's house arrest should be suspended pending legal review, says A-GC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has called for a temporary suspension of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest pending clarification on the interpretation of his conditional royal pardon.
The A-GC, in a statement, said Najib's existing detention status should be maintained until the legal issues surrounding the pardon and the High Court's order for his release were resolved.
The statement came hours after Umno settled Najib's RM50 million fine and the High Court issued an order of discharge on payment of the fine, directing his immediate release while requiring him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The A-GC said two possible interpretations had arisen from the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, on Sept 18.
"First, the payment of the RM50 million fine only fulfils the fine component of the sentence, while the prison sentence for the SRC International case remains in force until Aug 23, 2028.
"Under this interpretation, house arrest is an alternative method or place for serving the remainder of the prison sentence, and not the termination of the prison sentence," it said.
The A-GC said the second interpretation was that payment of the RM50 million fine could result in the entire SRC International sentence, including the prison term, being considered completed.
"The issue also involves the legal effect of the Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine dated Nov 6, 2026, issued by the High Court after the payment of the RM50 million fine was recorded.
"The order directs that Najib be released immediately, but at the same time states that the remainder of his sentence must be served under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, pursuant to the conditional pardon," it said.
The A-GC said the legal questions also had implications for Najib's separate 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) prison sentence, which was ordered to begin after the completion of his SRC International sentence.
It said the matter required further examination, particularly as the High Court had dismissed Najib's application for a stay of execution in the 1MDB case on Oct 14.
"Given that the issues raised involve complex legal questions, have implications for the implementation of the royal pardon and court orders, and represent an unprecedented situation, the A-GC is of the view that clear and definitive legal clarification must be obtained before further implementation measures are taken," it said.
The A-GC said the implementation of Najib's house arrest should therefore be temporarily deferred until the interpretation of the conditional pardon and the effect of the court's discharge order had been clarified.
"During this period, his detention status should be maintained at his existing place of detention, subject to the powers and directions of the relevant authorities," it said.
The A-GC stressed that the temporary deferment was not intended to challenge or disregard the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's decree.
"Instead, it is a measure to ensure that the royal decree and related court orders are implemented properly, systematically and in accordance with the true legal position," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 69 items named National Heritage 2026, from traditional foods to historic artefacts
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 69 items have been recognised as National Heritage 2026, including popular traditional foods such as uthappam, mi kolok, and kek lapis.
Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said 39 items have been declared to date, while another 30 will be gazetted later.
In a statement marking the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026, he said the list reflects Malaysia's cultural diversity.
"The total includes heritage items recognised as part of efforts to preserve and protect the nation's heritage, covering tangible and intangible heritage as well as recipients of the Living National Heritage Award," he said.
Chiew said 11 figures were recognised and would receive National Heritage certificates, RM20,000 in cash, and incentives from the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry.
Those honoured included Che Mohd Nasir Yusoff for his contributions to Kelantan shadow puppetry, Salbiah Muhi for keringkam embroidery, and Siow Ho Phiew for lion dance performances and lion head craftsmanship.
Sixteen heritage objects were also accorded National Heritage status. They include the Terengganu Quran manuscript, the Dewan Rakyat mace dating from 1952, the Dewan Negara mace used in 1966, and the table used for the first cabinet meeting chaired by Tunku Abdul Rahman.
Chiew said the remaining 30 heritage items to be gazetted include the Gawai Dayak Festival, Adat Berkadim, and the pending.
"The list also features traditional Malaysian dishes such as kacang pool, nasi kandar, apam Johol, kuih chang, char kue kak, and pasembur," he said.
Other items on the list include Malaysian Breakfast Culture, Tadau Kaamatan, Baba Nyonya wedding customs, Tahnik, copper craft, traditional clogs, tajau, sompoton, Kain Punca Potong, Kain Limar Tenggarung, Baju Sikap, Hikayat Puteri Saadong, the Mahsuri Legend, the Legend of Puteri Santubong, and Tuhfat Al-Nafis.
Chiew said the declaration of National Heritage is an important legal responsibility under the National Heritage Act 2005 [Act 645], which entrusts the Heritage Commissioner with screening, research, and technical assessments.
"However, the law stipulates that the final authority to declare an item as National Heritage rests with the minister.
"This mandate carries great significance. The declaration is not merely about conferring a name or title, but represents the highest form of recognition by the federal government," he said.
He said all National Heritage items would enjoy legal protection, be prioritised in preservation efforts, and receive government support for conservation.
Chiew said tourism centred on cultural heritage could generate income for arts practitioners, craft businesses, and local communities.
"However, efforts to develop this potential must go hand in hand with preserving the authenticity and value of our heritage," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher acquitted of three sexual assault charges involving students
Article:
TAWAU: The Sessions Court acquitted and discharged a teacher of three counts of sexual assault involving three female students three years ago.
Judge Ahmad Faizadh Yahaya made the decision after ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Sanyzam Dabal, 49.
The court also ordered that Sanyzam's bail money be returned.
In his judgment, Ahmad Faizadh said the time frames specified in the first and second charges were too broad, prejudicing the accused's ability to raise an alibi defence.
He said other prosecution witnesses did not support the testimony of two of the victims and also contradicted their interviews recorded at the Child Interview Centre, the testimony of one victim's mother and the evidence of the investigating officer.
The judge said investigators also failed to call a pupil who allegedly witnessed one of the incidents to testify in court, despite having recorded a statement from the child.
The investigating officer also failed to inspect or retrieve an "MMI" book mentioned by one of the victims in her testimony.
The victim had testified that the sexual harassment occurred during an Islamic education lesson after she failed to complete the MMI book.
The court also noted that the investigating officer failed to question two pupils who were said to have accompanied the victim when she reported the incident to her mother, as well as several Year Six pupils who allegedly informed a teacher about the matter.
Ahmad Faizadh said Sanyzam had told the investigating officer in his statement that he had never instructed anyone to write in the MMI book.
However, investigators did not pursue the matter, which the judge said demonstrated lapses in the police probe.
Sanyzam was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act with three counts of committing physical sexual assault against three female pupils at the school where he taught between March and November 2023.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN manifesto launch: PN shows support, signals united front for Melaka polls
Article:
AYER KEROH: A sea of blue and green filled the grounds of the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) this evening as supporters and party machinery from Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) gathered for the launch of BN's manifesto for the 16th Melaka state election.
An estimated 5,000 supporters and grassroots campaign workers gathered at the convention hall for the launch, reflecting the scale of the two coalitions' mobilisation ahead of the state election.
Supporters carrying BN's dacing flags and PN banners began arriving as early as 3pm, filling parking areas and surrounding access roads around MITC.
[[nid:1572280]]
Supporters from both coalitions filled the venue, their flags and banners reflecting the cooperation between the two sides as their grassroots machinery came together in a public display of unity ahead of the state election.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh unveiled the election manifesto at 5pm. Drawn up with input from Perikatan Nasional, it outlined the alliance's socioeconomic pledges, welfare schemes and infrastructure plans ahead of polling day.
Rather than contesting against each other in multi-cornered fights, the two coalitions negotiated seat allocations across the 28 State Legislative Assembly (DUN) constituencies.
