Title: Melaka polls: BN, Perikatan pledge RM30b investments, free water and no quit rent hike in joint manifesto
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 6 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched a joint manifesto for the 16th Melaka state election.
State BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto, themed “Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara”, outlines 113 initiatives focusing on the cost of living, income, housing and the future of families.
He said the economic initiatives include a target to attract up to RM30 billion in investments, particularly in new development areas and high-tech industries.
“We are also offering one-off financial assistance to children from B40 families in Melaka to pursue Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) certification programmes, while aiming to establish the state as a national TVET hub.
“We are also committed to providing free water for domestic consumption below 20,000 cubic metres a month, no increase in quit rent for five years and offering business funding assistance to small traders,” he said at the launch of the manifesto in Ayer Keroh here today.
Also present were Umno vice-president and Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said BN had fulfilled up to 97 per cent of the pledges made in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.
A total of 28 state seats are up for grabs in the election, with BN contesting 23 seats and PN the remaining five.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan warns heavy vehicle drivers to check blind spots as Deepavali traffic builds
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — Drivers of heavy vehicles using highways in Negeri Sembilan are reminded to be more mindful of blind spots and to ensure their surroundings are clear before changing lanes, in order to prevent accidents especially during the upcoming Deepavali festive season.
Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (RTD) director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said blind spots on heavy vehicles are a frequent cause of accidents, often occurring when drivers fail to check their side mirrors thoroughly, meanwhile, smaller vehicles following too closely also face significant risks.
He noted that areas in the state with high concentrations of heavy vehicle traffic include Kilometre 269 and KM 258 of the PLUS Highway, as well as the roads connecting Ulu Bendul–Terachi, Seremban–Tampin, Seremban–Lukut, Batang Benar–Nilai, Gemencheh and the Bahau–Rompin road.
“The implementation of ‘Op Patuh’ focuses on high-risk traffic violations, including speeding, running red lights, overtaking across double lines, cutting queues, misusing emergency lanes, carrying dangerous loads, and failing to wear seatbelts or motorcycle helmets.
“Traffic volume is expected to double, an increase of 100 per cent. Additionally, aerial monitoring will be conducted using two drones, operated by specialised personnel, to detect traffic offenders at intersections and along critical stretches of road,” he told reporters today at the Road Safety Campaign held in conjunction with the 2026 Deepavali celebrations.
Jasyindar noted that the use of mobile phones while driving, as well as the risk of drivers experiencing “microsleep” due to fatigue, are also key areas of focus for this operation, as these factors can lead to fatal accidents.
He said the department will optimise its personnel deployment for “Op Patuh,” which will run from November 7 to 12.
Furthermore, he mentioned that in addition to road patrols, plainclothes enforcement officers will be deployed at public bus terminals to investigate complaints regarding express bus services.
“These measures include ensuring that no passengers are standing on board, preventing the drop-off of passengers in unauthorised locations, and verifying the physical fitness of drivers,” he said.
He emphasised that these enforcement efforts are not intended solely for issuing summonses as they are aimed at preventing accidents and ensure that road users consistently adhere to traffic regulations. — Bernama

Title: Terminal Bersepadu Selatan expects 175,000 passengers over Deepavali travel period, up 20pc
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) is expected to receive approximately 175,000 passengers throughout this year’s Deepavali festive period, a 20 per cent increase compared to the same festive season last year.
TMAS Sdn Bhd Chief Executive Officer Shazwan Mohammad said the figure is expected to be recorded over a seven-day period starting yesterday until November 11, with an average of about 25,000 passengers per day.
He said that to ensure smooth operations during the period, TMAS as the operator of TBS will add personnel, including hiring part-time staff to assist with operational smoothness at TBS.
“We are also asking online ticket agents (OTAs) to send their own personnel to facilitate matters for passengers who purchase tickets through their respective platforms,” he said at a media session with Bernama at TBS here today.
Shazwan said TBS also expects a total of 10,000 bus departures and more than 4,000 bus arrivals throughout the period.
He said the surge in demand is also influenced by school holidays and the presence of foreign tourists who purchase tickets at the last minute.
He noted that routes to the East Coast are among those in high demand, and tickets to several destinations have even sold out as of this morning, though additional trips will be opened to accommodate demand.
Regarding ticket management, Shazwan said all ticket sales and travel information must be communicated to the terminal in accordance with the new Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) policy which came into effect on November 1.
He said the policy does not affect online ticket purchases; instead, the coordination of such information helps the terminal manage travel schedules and bus departures.
According to him, out of the average 18,000 tickets sold daily on ordinary days, about 4,000 are purchased via the terminal’s portal while the rest are through external platforms.
In the meantime, Shazwan reminded passengers who purchase tickets through OTAs to ensure they receive a QR-coded boarding pass to enter the departure lounge and board the bus.
He said tickets purchased through these platforms sometimes do not include the pass due to system differences between the OTA service providers and the terminal, thereby complicating information coordination and the issuance of boarding passes.
“Passengers who have not received a QR code need to contact the OTA where they purchased their tickets to obtain a boarding pass, but the process can take time if the travel information has not yet been entered into the terminal’s system,” he said.
Shazwan suggested purchasing tickets via the TBS app or website as well as the ticket kiosks available at the terminal and advised passengers to arrive earlier during the festive season, taking into account traffic conditions, terminal congestion, and the extra time needed to complete boarding pass procedures, especially for purchases that did not come with a departure QR code. — Bernama

Title: Six MACC strategic communications officers receive IPRM accreditation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Six officers from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Strategic Communications Division (BKS) have received the Accreditation in Public Relations (APR) award from the Institute of Public Relations Malaysia (IPRM).
The MACC said in a statement that all six recipients completed their accreditation requirements, which included passing and executing a public relations (PR) case study or research publication, attending an interview session, and completing documentation.
Among the recipients honoured at Menara Komunikasi here yesterday were BKS director Hisyam Mohd Yusoff, deputy director Badrila Jamlus, and Multimedia Branch head Azrai Mohammad.
Meanwhile, Information Department (JaPen) director-general Erwin Khairul Ahmad said in the same statement that the IPRM continues to play an important role in strengthening the public relations profession in Malaysia since its establishment in 1962.
“Careers in communication will not become obsolete and will endure, especially in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). Although the profession faces growing challenges in an AI-driven world, it still requires the human touch to manage communication strategically, particularly on social media, so that it is more meaningful, ethical, and effective.
“While AI is capable of generating text or drafting quickly, technology lacks core elements such as empathy and integrity, which are essential in professional communication,” he said.
IPRM president Jaffri Amin Osman said that for the first time, all IPRM APR recipients will be recognised to conduct training or coaching by public relations institutes across several Asean countries, including Indonesia, Singapore, and the Philippines.
He said the awards are expected to continue raising professional standards, strengthen strategic communications expertise, and elevate Malaysia’s public relations industry to greater heights. — Bernama

Title: Bright light seen in Malaysian airspace linked to Nasa satellite re-entry, no debris found, says Mosti
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — The Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti), through the Space Authority Division (BPAngkasa), confirmed receiving preliminary information on reports of bright light sightings in Malaysian airspace over several areas on Wednesday night (November 4).
In a statement today, Mosti said the sightings were also linked to the re-entry of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (Nasa) Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory satellite.
“So far, there are no official reports on the discovery of any suspected space object debris, such as rockets, on land or in Malaysian waters,” the statement read.
Mosti added that active monitoring is being conducted by BPAngkasa in collaboration with relevant agencies.
The public is advised not to touch any suspicious objects and to report them immediately to the authorities, the 999 emergency line, or directly to BPAngkasa at 03-8885 8685 or bpadg@mosti.gov.my.
“Mosti also urges the public not to make any speculations and to obtain authentic information from official channels,” it added. — Bernama

Title: AGC says Najib’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) says the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification on the interpretation of his conditional pardon and the effect of a High Court order issued today.
In a statement, the AGC said Najib’s detention status should remain unchanged at his existing place of detention while the legal issues were being examined.
The conditional pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim on September 18, 2026 allowed Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and compliance with the stipulated conditions.
However, the AGC said two possible interpretations had arisen over whether payment of the fine meant Najib’s prison sentence in the SRC International case remained in force or was considered completed.
Under the first interpretation, payment of the RM50 million fine would fulfil only the financial component of the sentence, while the prison term would continue until August 23, 2028.
House arrest would therefore be an alternative means of serving the remaining prison term, rather than an indication that the sentence had ended.
Under the second interpretation, payment of the fine would allow the pardon to take full effect, meaning the entire sentence for the SRC International case, including the prison term, would be considered completed.
The AGC said the issue also involved the legal effect of an Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court today after the RM50 million payment was recorded.
The order directed Najib’s immediate release, while also stating that the remainder of his sentence should be served under house arrest until August 23, 2028 in accordance with the conditional pardon.
The interpretation of Najib’s remaining prison term in the SRC International case could also affect the implementation of his sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case, the AGC said.
This is because a court order stipulates that the 1MDB prison sentence must begin after the completion of his sentence in the SRC International case.
The AGC said the matter also needed to be examined in light of the High Court’s rejection on October 14, 2026 of Najib’s application for a stay of execution of his sentence in the 1MDB case.
Describing the issues as legally complex and unprecedented, the AGC said clear and definitive legal clarification was necessary before any further implementation action could be taken.
It said the proposed temporary postponement was not intended to challenge or set aside the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s decree, but to ensure that the royal pardon and related court orders were implemented accurately and in accordance with the actual legal position.
The AGC said it would take further action once the review and clarification had been completed.

Title: Najib taken for scheduled dental examination after leaving Kajang Prison, Anthony Loke says
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to return home after leaving Kajang Prison today, as he was taken to a dental clinic for a scheduled examination, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said.
Loke, who earlier announced his resignation as transport minister, said he received the information from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
“The Home Minister had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home.
“I was told that Najib had been taken to a dental clinic for an examination as scheduled,” he said.
Earlier today, the Kuala Lumpur High Court issued an Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine after Najib settled the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case, with the order stating that the remainder of his sentence should be served under house arrest.
The fine was paid using funds raised by the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, which was launched by Umno on September 18 and had successfully reached its collection target.
Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International.
He was initially sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
However, the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced his sentence in January 2024 to six years’ imprisonment and a RM50 million fine.
On September 18, the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the stipulated conditions.

Title: Penang committed to sustainable, well-regulated pig farming, says state exco
Article:
TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 6 — The Penang state government is committed to ensuring that the pig farming industry in the state continues to be managed in an orderly and sustainable manner through more systematic management, close monitoring and effective enforcement of regulations.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said this approach would allow the industry to continue operating and growing in line with legal requirements and standards without compromising environmental sustainability.
“The state government has never shied away from acknowledging the pollution caused by improper management of pig farming waste in the past; instead, we have taken corrective measures to ensure the issue is addressed comprehensively.
“As a responsible state government, we are prepared to admit our shortcomings, confront the problems and seek solutions, rather than evade responsibility or eliminate the industry as a way out,” he said in a statement today.
He was responding to Tasek Gelugor MP Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan’s call for the pig farms in Kampung Selamat to be closed immediately during a recent parliamentary debate.
H’ng highlighted that the state government is carrying out proactive measures to address pollution in Sungai Kereh, particularly to restore and improve the river’s water quality.
These efforts, he added, have also drawn recognition from Permatang Berangan assemblyman Mohd Sobri Saleh during a recent state legislative assembly sitting.
He said the state government had also introduced new regulations requiring breeders to upgrade their technology, knowledge and expertise, particularly in environmental cleanliness, waste management and effluent discharge control.
At the same time, he said, breeders are given reasonable space and opportunity to upgrade their technology and farm management practices to meet higher environmental protection standards, while the pig farming industry contributes to the agricultural production sector and stimulates the supply chain.
Responding to Wan Saiful’s suggestion that the government helps breeders transition to other economic sectors through training and assistance, he opined that such an approach would indirectly still lead to the closure of the industry as its ultimate goal.
Accordingly, he urged the MP to obtain a more comprehensive picture of the state government’s efforts and actions before making statements on the pig farming and pollution issue in Seberang Perai Utara. — Bernama

Title: Financially vulnerable Malaysians targeted for recruitment as drug mules, police say
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Individuals with financial difficulties, especially those from Sarawak and Pahang, have been targeted by international drug smuggling rings to be recruited as drug mules.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicate’s activities were exposed following the arrest of four individuals, including the foreign mastermind, in Brickfields here yesterday.
The suspects, three locals acting as recruiters and the mastermind, a man holding a Hong Kong passport, who supplied the drugs, were arrested at a homestay in Brickfields, he added.
“Two pairs of shoes and 450 grams of cocaine believed destined for two drug mules were also seized,” he said at a media conference here today, adding the the local men were arrested under Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
The syndicate has been identified for recruiting five Malaysians arrested by authorities in Soekarno-Hatta  International Airport in Jakarta, Indonesia and five others in Haneda International Airport in Tokyo, Japan in September and October.
In a separate case, Hussein said police seized 109.17 kilogrammes of cannabis and arrested a man in Selangor on October 30, and seized two cars, a motorcycle and various jewellery items.
The man, who tested positive for drugs and has three previous criminal records, has been remanded till November 12 under section 38B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia declares 69 items National Heritage, from ‘mi kolok’ to Dewan Rakyat mace
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — A total of 69 heritage items have been recognised as National Heritage 2026, including
uthappam
,
mi kolok
and
kek lapis
, popular foods that reflect Malaysia’s cultural diversity, Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said.
In a statement marking the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026, he said 39 heritage items had been declared to date, while a further 30 would be gazetted later.
“The total includes heritage items recognised as part of efforts to preserve and protect the nation’s heritage, covering tangible and intangible heritage as well as recipients of the Living National Heritage Award (WAKOH),” he said.
A total of 11 figures were also recognised and would receive National Heritage certificates, RM20,000 in cash and incentives from the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac), he said.
Those honoured included Che Mohd Nasir Yusoff for his efforts in Kelantan shadow puppetry, Salbiah Muhi for
keringkam
embroidery, and Siow Ho Phiew for lion dance performances and lion head craftsmanship.
Sixteen heritage objects were also accorded National Heritage status, including the Terengganu Quran manuscript, the Dewan Rakyat mace dating from 1952, the Dewan Negara mace used in 1966, and the table used for the first Cabinet meeting chaired by Tunku Abdul Rahman.
“The remaining 30 heritage items will be gazetted in due course. They include the Gawai Dayak Festival, the Adat Berkadim (joining a ritual practice) and the
pending
(Malay ornamental belt buckle).
“The list also features traditional Malaysian dishes such as
kacang pool
,
nasi kandar
,
apam Johol
,
kuih chang
,
char kue kak
and
pasembur
,” he said.
Other items on the cultural heritage list are Malaysian Breakfast Culture, Tadau Kaamatan (annual harvest festival), Baba Nyonya wedding customs, Tahnik (a traditional Islamic practice of touching a newborn baby’s palate with a softened date or honey), copper craft, traditional clogs, tajau (heirloom jar),
sompoton
(Sabah mouth organ), Kain Punca Potong (handwoven textile fabric), Kain Limar Tenggarung (Malay traditional woven textile), Baju Sikap (royal outer coat), Hikayat Puteri Saadong, the Mahsuri Legend, the Legend of Puteri Santubong and Tuhfat Al-Nafis (19th-century Malay historical chronicle).
Chiew said the declaration of National Heritage is an important legal responsibility under the National Heritage Act 2005 [Act 645], which entrusts the Heritage Commissioner with screening, research and technical assessments.
“However, the law stipulates that the final authority to declare an item as National Heritage rests with the Minister.
“This mandate carries great significance. The declaration is not merely about conferring a name or title, but represents the highest form of recognition by the federal government,” he said, noting that all National Heritage items would enjoy legal protection, be prioritised in preservation efforts and receive government support for conservation.
Chiew also emphasised that tourism centred on cultural heritage could generate income for arts practitioners, craft businesses and local communities.
“However, efforts to develop this potential must go hand in hand with preserving the authenticity and value of our heritage,” he said. — Bernama

Title: OPR stays at 2.75pc as Bank Negara sees no need to tighten monetary policy, says governor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent reflects its assessment that the rate remains consistent with price stability outlook and sustainable economic growth, said Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.
“When we assess the growth and inflation outlook, we see that the current OPR level of 2.75 per cent remains consistent with our assessment of the economic outlook,” he told Bernama after the OPR announcement yesterday.
Abdul Rasheed said global growth demonstrated resilience, supported by factors such as the continued expansion of technology-related investments and strong demand associated with the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.
He said Malaysia’s economy demonstrated resilience in sustaining growth, with the third-quarter (3Q) advance estimate recording a 5.3 per cent expansion and average growth for the first three quarters reaching 5.6 per cent.
He said domestic demand remained supported by sustained household spending, ongoing structural reforms and investment activities, while exports continued to benefit from strong demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products, supported by the global AI and technology upcycle.
Against this backdrop, the governor said the central bank saw no immediate need to tighten policy as inflation remains contained.
Nevertheless, the MPC is vigilant about signs of broader price pressures and has the flexibility to adjust policy when needed.
BNM is also monitoring wage increases because stronger household purchasing power could potentially generate additional demand and put pressure on prices.
“If we see pressure on prices as wages increase, thus changing the inflation trajectory, an adjustment may be necessary to ensure monetary policy remains consistent with the growth and inflation outlook,” he said.
Abdul Rasheed said Malaysia’s economic growth is expected to exceed five per cent this year while the outlook for 2027 remains positive, supported by resilient domestic demand, ongoing investment activities and sustained external demand, particularly for technology-related products.
He added that while the 2027 growth trajectory remains strong, some moderation would be expected.
“Domestic demand is expected to remain supported by improving household incomes, continued structural reforms and measures under Budget 2027,” he said, adding that the global AI and technology upcycle, as well as demand for data centres, would remain important growth drivers next year.
He emphasised that Malaysia’s diversified economy and solid buffers will also help the country weather global uncertainties.
Investments from previous years are being realised, further supporting growth and new investments are also expected to have a higher multiplier impact on the economy.
Nonetheless, inflation is expected to edge higher next year — between 1.8 and 2.8 per cent — compared with 1.5 to 2.5 per cent this year amid global inflation as input prices remain elevated. — Bernama

Title: Transport Minister Anthony Loke resigns as Najib returns home to begin house arrest
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook has announced his resignation after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
Loke said his stance on the matter had not changed and that his resignation would take effect the moment Najib arrives home.
“I would like to record my appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the trust and mandate given to me throughout my 47 months serving as Transport Minister, from December 2022 until today,” he said at a press conference.
Loke said he had been informed that the RM50 million payment issue involving Najib had been settled at the High Court this morning and that he would be released from prison.
“However, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home,” he said.
He added he had also received confirmation that Najib had been taken to a dental clinic for an examination, as scheduled, following media reports that the former prime minister had left Kajang Prison.
Loke reiterated that his resignation would take effect immediately once Najib arrived at his residence, adding that he would submit an additional letter to Anwar to formalise the matter.
“My resignation letter had already been submitted earlier and my position remained unchanged,” he said.
Asked whether Anwar had contacted him over the matter, Loke said they had spoken after the Cabinet meeting, but maintained that he would remain consistent with his earlier position.
“This is my party’s decision and I will abide by it,” he added.
Meanwhile, Loke said he had chaired a post-Cabinet meeting at the Transport Ministry today to settle administrative matters and ensure a smooth transition of duties.
“Although, my resignation will take effect immediately once Najib arrives home, I have already been invited by the Ministry’s secretary-general Datuk Seri M. Jana Santhiran to attend the Deepavali celebration next Wednesday.
“Therefore, I will return on Wednesday and that may also be my last official engagement with the ministry,” he said.
He also expressed his appreciation to the ministry’s secretary-general, deputy secretaries-general, division secretaries and all ministry officials for their cooperation and support throughout his tenure.
On the ministry’s ongoing plans and initiatives, Loke said all programmes would continue as scheduled, expressing confidence in the ability of its officers to ensure continuity.
Among the initiatives, he said the MyKomuter50 programme would be launched by December, while East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) was scheduled to begin operations on December 12.
He added that the Rapid Transit System (RTS) project was also scheduled to begin in February.
Loke said he would continue supporting the ministry even after leaving the Cabinet, as he would remain a Member of Parliament.
“I am still a Member of Parliament, so I will continue to provide support to the ministry’s officers. Whatever I can help with or contribute, I will do so,” he said.

Title: Zahid reminds Loke of pledge to resign from Cabinet post if Najib is released for house arrest today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Transport Minister Anthony Loke to step down today if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is released following the settlement of his RM50 million fine.
Zahid said Loke must honour his pledge, according to a
New Straits Times
report.
“I hope he will fulfil his promise. I think this is not merely a political statement,” he said at a press conference in Istanbul.
“He must do it immediately if Datuk Seri Najib is released today.”
Zahid is in Istanbul for a four-day working visit to Turkiye, where he is attending the TRT World Forum 2026 as a panellist and holding meetings focused on TVET and education cooperation.
The challenge comes after Umno confirmed that the fine had been paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, paving the way for house arrest under Najib’s conditional pardon.
Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon on September 18, permitting him to serve the rest of his term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the fine and other conditions are met.
Loke had said on September 29 that he submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, but was asked to remain in office temporarily.
Najib, 73, has been at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine, which the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.

Title: MetMalaysia forecasts continuous rain in Kelantan, Terengganu from Sunday to Nov 11
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Continuous rain is expected in several parts of Kelantan and Terengganu from Sunday until Nov 11, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the affected areas in Kelantan include Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok and Pasir Puteh.
In Terengganu, continuous rain is expected to affect Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu, Marang and Hulu Terengganu, he said.
Mohd Hisham said continuous rain is also forecast in Sabah from Nov 9 to 11, covering Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Kinabatangan in the Sandakan division.
“Analysis of weather forecast models indicates that a monsoon surge is expected to affect the country from Nov 9 to 11, potentially bringing continuous heavy rain to the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia and eastern Sabah,” he said.
The public can obtain the latest weather updates through MetMalaysia’s official website, social media channels and the myCuaca mobile application, or contact the department’s hotline at 1-300-22-1638 for further enquiries. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia assessing impact of US midterm election results, including tariffs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government is examining the short and medium-term impacts across various aspects following political developments in the United States (US), where the Republican Party suffered a defeat in the midterm elections on Tuesday.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed in depth during today’s Cabinet meeting and Malaysia will continue to monitor the situation, including potential implications regarding the implementation of reciprocal tariffs.
“…however, our relations with the current administration, the existing government, as well as both incumbent and newly elected members of Congress including the House of Representatives will continue,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Taman Kosas Mosque, near here, today.
The Republican Party, led by President Donald Trump, was reportedly defeated by the Democratic Party, which secured control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections on Tuesday.
Offering a personal perspective on these developments, Anwar welcomed the shift, viewing it as a rejection by the electorate of politics rooted in racial and religious hatred including anti-Islamic sentiment and hostility toward minority groups.
“From a global standpoint, I see this as a positive signal, many [of those elected] oppose attacks and hostility toward Islam, as well as hostility toward Iran. Hopefully, this will help ease international geopolitical tensions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PM disagrees with Umno’s RM50m fine payment for Najib, but respects legal process
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed disagreement with Umno’s decision to pay the RM50 million fine on behalf of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, stressing that corruption and abuse of power must not be taken lightly in the name of friendship.
Anwar said personal ties and goodwill towards Najib should not create the impression that corruption and abuse of power involving billions of ringgit could be overlooked.
However, he acknowledged that the payment was Umno’s prerogative, adding that the government respected the legal process and His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia’s decision under the Constitution.
“Personally, I disagree. While we have a sense of friendship with Datuk Seri Najib, it must not give the public the impression that corruption involving billions of ringgit can simply be overlooked.
“What values are we teaching our children? We must uphold firm moral principles that reject abuse of power and corruption,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Taman Kosas here today.
Earlier, Umno announced the closure of its special Najib Razak Solidarity Fund account after public contributions reached the required amount.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said in a statement that the party had completed all payment procedures with the Kuala Lumpur High Court this morning.
He said the fund, launched on September 18, was established to collect public donations through crowdfunding to assist the former prime minister and Umno president.
Najib was reported to have settled the RM50 million fine imposed in his SRC International Sdn Bhd fund misappropriation case at the High Court’s criminal registry today.
His special officer, Ahmad Lutfi Azhar, arrived at the court at 11.30am to arrange the payment and complete the necessary administrative procedures.
The payment was among the conditions of a royal pardon granted on September 18, allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds. — Bernama

Title: Cabinet approves transfer of scheduled waste management powers to Sarawak under MA63
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Cabinet has agreed to a memorandum on amendments to the Borneo States (Legislative Powers) Order for Sarawak, paving the way for the transfer of scheduled waste management powers to the state government under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
Madani government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the memorandum, submitted by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), was agreed upon at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the proposed amendments had received clearance from the Attorney-General’s Chambers and would next be submitted for royal consent from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
“This decision reflects the Prime Minister’s and government’s commitment to strengthening the implementation of MA63, particularly by ensuring that federal legislative powers are conferred on the Sarawak government in an orderly and effective manner, in accordance with Article 95C of the Federal Constitution,” he said in a statement today.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the amendment was a crucial step before the application of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (Act 127) is suspended in Sarawak to enable the state government to assume responsibility for scheduled waste management.
The move, he said, would also prevent overlapping jurisdiction between the federal and Sarawak governments.
Fahmi also said the transfer of federal legislative powers in environmental matters to Sabah and Sarawak would be implemented in phases, beginning with scheduled waste management, he added.
“The Government remains committed to translating the MA63 agenda into concrete actions and decisions to strengthen federal-state relations and safeguard the interests of the people of Sabah and Sarawak,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Najib exits Kajang Prison to serve out SRC sentence under house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Malaysia’s former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left prison on Friday after paying a fine that allows him to serve the rest of his sentence at home, an AFP reporter saw.
Najib, 73, was whisked from Kajang Prison in a silver car followed by a convoy of vehicles, according to an AFP reporter at the scene.

Title: Teo Nie Ching urges govt agencies to conduct cybersecurity audits amid rising hacking threats
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 6 — All government agencies must conduct cybersecurity audits to identify vulnerabilities in their respective digital systems and infrastructure amid heightened hacking threats linked to developments in international conflicts.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the measure was crucial to ensuring that security systems, including firewalls, could effectively protect data and prevent intrusions by unscrupulous parties.
She said that while the National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) led the country’s cybersecurity efforts, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) was ready to assist government agencies in conducting the audits.
“We have therefore asked the MCMC to assist in conducting cybersecurity audits to ensure that existing systems are not easily breached by hackers,” she said after presenting a contribution under the Tabung Kasih@HAWANA X TM initiative to a former Utusan Malaysia photographer here today.
Teo said efforts to strengthen cybersecurity should also extend to the private sector, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and associations, particularly those that rely on the internet and store data online.
She said all organisations, particularly those operating critical infrastructure such as hospitals and banking systems, should allocate dedicated funds for cybersecurity audits.
Teo said previous hacking incidents targeting local authority systems highlighted the importance of preventive measures and safeguarding digital data.
“Just as people are encouraged to undergo health check-ups, companies, NGOs and associations must also give due attention to cybersecurity,” she said.
She also advised organisations subscribing to artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing services to set aside part of their budgets to strengthen cybersecurity.
Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the Royal Malaysia Police continued to strengthen its preparedness against potential cyber threats amid developments in international conflicts, particularly those involving Iran and the United States. — Bernama

Title: Selangor to review approved projects, tighten flood mitigation requirements in high-risk areas
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR, Nov 6  — The Selangor state government will order a review of previously approved development projects to ensure that flood mitigation systems are implemented in high-risk areas.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari saId this measure is part of the state government’s efforts to reduce flood risks and prevent a recurrence of such incidents in the affected areas.
“I will request a review of all approvals we have granted, including imposing a requirement for developers to construct temporary water retention facilities; we certainly do not want them to carry out the work in a shoddy or substandard manner,” he said.
He made these remarks when met after inspecting a retention pond site at the Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Puncak Alam campus here today.
Amirudin added that the state government has also identified several other issues contributing to flooding in areas such as Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching, and Bukit Hijau.
He saId identified issues include acts of vandalism along the embankments of the Sungai Buloh 1 Flood Mitigation Scheme (RTB) where the structures have been lowered below their original specifications as well as water overflow originating from the West Coast Expressway (WCE).
“I have requested that the vandalism issue be addressed immediately. We will take action against illegal operations in the area, and several demolition exercises will have to be carried out.
“These demolitions are necessary to gazette the sites as water catchment areas or floodplains two locations have already been identified for this purpose. The process will be executed by the District and Land Office in collaboration with the local authorities,” he said.
Meanwhile, addressing the case of a local mosque that frequently experiences flooding despite not being situated near a river, Amirudin noted that his administration would consult with the mosque’s management to discuss either raising the structure or relocating the place of worship to a more suitable site.
He explained that this occurs because the area is low-lying and receives overflow from the Subang River.
“This is overflow from the Subang River, which flows toward Merbau Sempak, eventually reaching the Sungai Buloh river system and arriving here. Ultimately, the water seeks an outlet to the sea but there is no sea here so the nearest coastline is in Kuala Selangor.
“This has long been the natural movement of water; runoff from Gombak or Petaling tends to flow toward the Ijok or Kuala Selangor areas and this has been the established pattern for a long time,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan Customs seizes RM2.56m in cigarettes, liquor and smuggled goods
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — The Negeri Sembilan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department crippled smuggling activities in two raids on Oct 26, seizing cigarettes, liquor and other goods with a total value of RM2.56 million, including duties.
Its director, Jamal Paiman, said the seizures by the Enforcement Division involved various items worth RM359,271, with duties amounting to RM2.2 million.
He said the items seized comprised 3,008,200 sticks of cigarettes of various brands, 2,910.64 litres of liquor, 221 electrical appliances and a packaging machine.
“In the first case, a team from the Operations Branch intercepted a Daihatsu van in an alley behind a row of shoplots in Taman Sejahtera, Kuala Lumpur, at about 3 pm. The van was believed to be used to distribute smuggled goods for the local market.
“An inspection found 10,000 packets, equivalent to 200,000 sticks, of cigarettes of various brands suspected to be prohibited imports under the Customs (Prohibition of Imports) Order 2023. The estimated value of the seized cigarettes and van was RM36,000, while the duties involved amounted to RM138,000,” he told a press conference here today.
He said a 42-year-old man was detained following the raid to assist in investigations.
Jamal said that in the second raid, his team inspected a building in the same area at 4 pm and found 1,370 bottles of liquor of various brands, 4,824 cans of alcoholic beverages, 244 boxes containing 2,808,200 sticks of cigarettes of various brands, and 221 assorted electrical appliances suspected to be smuggled goods.
He said all the items were seized under Section 114 of the Customs Act 1967, while the case was being investigated under Sections 135(1)(d) and 135(1)(e) of the same Act. — Bernama

Title: High Court orders Najib’s house arrest after Umno settles RM50m fine payment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The High Court has issued a house arrest order for Datuk Seri Najib Razak after his RM50 million fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was settled today.
Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, a member of Najib’s legal team, confirmed the payment was made by Umno to the High Court registry this morning, according to
The Star
.
“As of this morning, the RM50 million fine before Najib has been paid by Umno to the High Court,” he said during the press conference.
“As a result, the court has issued, pursuant to the royal pardon, the order of house arrest.”
Farhan said the legal team has obtained the house arrest order and will deliver it to Kajang Prison.
He noted that further processes remain before the former prime minister can be released from prison.
The payment was preceded by an announcement from Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who said this morning that the party had completed all payment processes to the court.
In a media statement, Asyraf Wajdi said the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund, launched on September 18, had reached its collection target and was sufficient.
He announced that the party had officially closed the special account, stating there was no longer any need for crowdfunding for the purpose.
Najib, 73, has been at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine, which the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.
Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon on September 18, permitting him to serve the rest of his term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the fine and other conditions are met.

Title: Johor Domestic Trade Ministry logs 2,373 offences, RM11.6m in seizures in price control crackdown
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 6 — The Johor Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) has recorded 2,373 offences, with seizures amounting to over RM11.6 million, from the start of the year until yesterday.
Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said that of this total, 1,774 cases involved offences under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011.
She said among the offences were the failure to display clear price tags or price lists for goods or services, selling controlled items above the stipulated maximum price and raising prices or profiteering in an unreasonable manner.
“During the same period, Johor KPDN also recorded 360 offences under the Weights and Measures Act 1972, 119 cases under the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and 66 offences under the Consumer Protection Act 1999,” she said during a state-level Festive Season Maximum Price Scheme (SHMMP) launch in conjunction with Deepavali 2026 at NSK Trade City in Skudai here today.
Lilis Saslinda said the ministry also detected 54 other offences under the Trademarks Act 2019, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Copyright Act 1987 and the Hire-Purchase Act 1967.
She noted that 879 offences were also detected out of 1,537 inspections conducted at the wholesale and retail levels during the implementation of the SHMMP for this year’s Chinese New Year and Hari Raya Aidilfitri celebrations.
Lilis Saslinda said the most frequently detected offense was the failure to display the required pink price tags for controlled items.
She urged traders to adhere to four key obligations during the SHMMP implementation: not selling controlled items above the maximum price, displaying pink price tags for controlled items, ensuring an adequate supply of goods in the market, and using approved weighing instruments and measuring scales.
“The Johor chapter of the ministry has taken proactive measures by intensifying advocacy efforts directed at traders.
“These were made through announcements on official social media channels, the distribution of leaflets on the list of controlled goods, as well as the responsibilities and obligations of traders,” she said.
In addition to the implementation of the SHMMP, Johor KPDN is continuing the Jualan Rahmah Madani outdoor initiative programme in conjunction with the festival at selected locations.
The programme begins today at Target Supermarket in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, the Benut multipurpose hall in Pontian, the Kota Tinggi Tourism and Transformation Centre and the IOI Mall Kulai field on November 7 and 8.

Title: ‘Payment completed’: Umno settles Najib’s RM50m fine, paving way for house arrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court for the RM50 million fine imposed on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, the party announced today.
Umno secretary-general Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said that the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund launched on September 18 had reached its collection target and was sufficient, according to the statement shared on his Facebook page.
“Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court this morning,” he said.
He also announced that the party had officially closed the special account established for public donations.
“Umno hereby officially closes the special Najib Razak Solidarity Fund account and no longer needs crowdfunding for this purpose,” he said.
Asyraf Wajdi expressed the party’s gratitude to Allah and thanked Umno members nationwide and the public who had contributed since the fund’s launch.
The statement did not disclose the total amount collected.
Najib, 73, has been at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine, which the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.
Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon on September 18, permitting him to serve the rest of his term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the fine and other conditions are met.

Title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast for six states and Putrajaya until 2pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across six states and the Federal Territory of Putrajaya, expected to last until 2pm today.
The warning, issued in a statement at noon today, covers Pahang (Kuantan and Rompin), Selangor (Sepang, Kuala Langat, Klang, Petaling and Kuala Selangor), Putrajaya, and Johor (Kota Tinggi and Mersing).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Mukah (Mukah, Dalat and Matu), Bintulu (Tatau and Bintulu), Sibu, Kapit (Song), Sri Aman (Lubok Antu) and Betong (Betong).
MetMalaysia said it issues such warnings when there are signs indicating thunderstorms with rain intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that are near or expected to occur for more than an hour.
“A thunderstorm warning is a short-term alert valid for a maximum of six hours for each release,” the department stated in its advisory.

Title: Najib’s lawyer, special officer enter KL Court Complex as RM50m fine payment speculation mounts
Article:

New Straits Times
report.
Lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee was seen entering the complex as speculation grew that the RM50 million fine could be settled, potentially allowing the former prime minister to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest.
Najib’s special officer, Ahmad Lutfi Azhar, had earlier arrived at 11.35am.
Lutfi told reporters at the court complex’s lobby that a statement would follow once matters were concluded.
Lutfi and Farhan were later seen entering the High Court Criminal Registry office together.

Title: Legal disputes cast doubt on year-end Petronas-Sarawak settlement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A year-end settlement between Sarawak and Petronas is not possible despite Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg expressing confidence that a deal could be reached before the end of the year, a political analyst said.
University of Tasmania’s James Chin said that, based on his knowledge and interactions in Sarawak, such an outcome was unlikely at present because the two sides remained fundamentally different in their interests, which is why they approached the Federal Court to resolve the deadlock in the first place.
“In that interview, although he mentioned that a deal is due by year-end, it is not possible to have the deal because court proceedings are ongoing.
“You cannot get an agreement while these court cases are happening unless Petronas withdraws, or both sides go to the courts and say they want to settle out of court,” Chin said.
Abang Johari told The Edge this week that the Petronas-Petros dispute was in its “last mile” and could be settled before the end of the year.
These negotiations come after two legal developments. Petronas filed its petition in January seeking clarity over the state and federal laws governing its operations in Sarawak. Sarawak then filed its own petition challenging the continued validity and application of several federal petroleum laws to the state.
The Federal Court has fixed Jan 25 to 29 next year to hear the two petitions, which are being kept separate and will be heard in the order in which they were filed.
The year-end target floated by the Sarawak premier also follows several earlier indications that an agreement was close.
In December last year, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said commercial negotiations were progressing well and that an outcome was expected in early 2026. He had earlier said only administrative and commercial issues remained unresolved.
By June this year, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said several important issues had been ironed out and a final agreement was expected soon, although analysts later cautioned that the continuing court cases showed that key legal and commercial questions remained unresolved.
Analysts say credibility in a deal could be undermined by continued promises without resolution.
“Missing the year-end target could raise questions about GPS’s credibility, particularly since Sarawak’s government had previously anticipated a commercial agreement by December 2025,” analyst Jamil Ghani said.
“Repeated assurances without tangible outcomes could gradually undermine confidence in the process.”
Universiti Malaya’s Azman Awang Pawi agreed that the deadline had created a benchmark against which the state government’s negotiating effectiveness could be judged.
“If the deadline passes without an agreement, opposition parties could question why a government with such a strong political mandate and considerable influence at the federal level has yet to secure a definitive settlement,” he said.
However, Azman cautioned against treating a missed deadline as a serious political setback in itself.
He said the dispute involved complex constitutional, regulatory and commercial questions which could not necessarily be resolved according to an electoral timetable, with the continuing legal proceedings themselves showing that important jurisdictional questions remained unsettled.
Azman said GPS also entered the election with considerable political capital built up through its wider autonomy agenda, development programmes and stable control of the state government.
A delayed agreement alone was therefore unlikely to seriously weaken the coalition.
“The greater risk emerges if negotiations repeatedly produce optimistic announcements without concrete implementation.”
Azman said Abang Johari’s standing would ultimately depend less on whether an agreement was signed by Dec 31 than on whether Sarawakians believed meaningful progress had been made without compromising the state’s long-term interests.
“If a final agreement is delayed but both sides can demonstrate clear consensus on regulatory responsibilities, commercial arrangements, Petros’s operational role and future revenue opportunities, the political damage may be limited,” he said.
Azman added that Sarawak’s petroleum aspirations and Petronas’s national mandate need not be mutually exclusive.
“The strongest outcome would be an agreement that converts constitutional disagreement into institutional cooperation, commercial certainty and greater economic benefits for Sarawak and Malaysia,” he said.
“That would be a stronger legacy for Abang Johari and GPS than any short-term electoral advantage gained from confrontation.”

Title: Police cordon off Najib’s Jalan Langgak Duta residence amid speculation of possible return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Police have tightened security at the entrance to Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here this morning, amid speculation that the former prime minister may return to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
Berita Harian
reported that Najib may be permitted to return home after settling the required payment.
Sentul district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam and his deputy were spotted arriving at the housing area at 10.45am, shortly after a team of officers and personnel from the district police headquarters turned up at 10.30am.
Police officers at the scene directed media personnel to keep their distance from the house, permitting coverage only from the junction leading into the residential area.
“Yes, we are making preparations for control and surveillance around the entrance to Datuk Seri Najib’s residence starting this morning,” Anuar Bakri told reporters.
“So far, we have not received any exact information, but we are preparing for any possibility.”
Close to 30 police personnel and several vehicles are currently on standby to monitor the area.
Anuar Bakri said officers had laid police tape to keep unauthorised individuals away from Najib’s home.
Checks by reporters found patrol cars and mobile vans deployed at the scene, along with two tents set up for duty and control purposes.
Information received indicates that Najib is expected back at his residence after Friday prayers this afternoon.
The presence of almost all senior Sentul district police officers at the location further suggests that Najib may be sent home today.
Najib, 73, has been at Kajang Prison since August 23, 2022, after the Federal Court upheld his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million from SRC International Sdn Bhd.
His original sentence was 12 years’ jail and a RM210 million fine, which the Federal Territories Pardons Board reduced in January 2024 to six years and RM50 million.
Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon on September 18, permitting him to serve the rest of his term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, provided the fine and other conditions are met.

Title: Three more held over fatal machete attack in Teluk Intan
Article:
IPOH, Nov 6 — Three more suspects have been arrested to assist in investigations into the death of a man who was believed to have been hacked with a machete in front of a shop in Taman Banjar Jaya, Teluk Intan, last Tuesday.
Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the three suspects were aged between their 30s and 40s.
“Two foreign men were arrested in the early hours of Nov 4 and remanded on the same day until Nov 11.
“A local man was also arrested yesterday, and police will apply for a remand order this morning. The case is still under investigation,” he said in a statement today.
On Nov 4, Chua said preliminary investigations found that the 48-year-old victim had been attacked by three men armed with machetes. The victim was rushed to Teluk Intan Hospital for treatment but was later pronounced dead by medical personnel.
Following the incident, police arrested a 27-year-old local woman, who was remanded until Nov 11 to assist in the investigation. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. — Bernama

Title: MyJPJ data not shared with insurance partner Nile Tech, says MOT
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Nile Tech Sdn Bhd has not been granted access to MyJPJ application’s database, and no user profile information is automatically transmitted to the company via the insurance renewal link within the application.
In a written response published on the Parliament website, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) clarified that the insurance renewal service featured in MyJPJ serves merely as a link, directing users to the Nile Tech portal to complete their transactions.
“When the link is selected, users are redirected from the MyJPJ application to the Nile Tech portal. All insurance renewal processes and transactions take place on that portal.
“Should a user choose to proceed on the Nile Tech portal, any information entered by the user is subject to the portal’s own terms, conditions, and privacy policy,” the Ministry said in response to a question from Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) regarding the protective measures in place to ensure that users’ personal data is not accessed by third parties.
The Ministry further explained that Nile Tech was appointed as a platform provider to offer an alternative channel for vehicle insurance renewal to MyJPJ users, aiming to facilitate online transactions and reduce the need for users to visit physical counters.
“This appointment was carried out through a process established by the MOT and the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and is subject to stipulated terms and conditions.
“The company has not been granted exclusive rights to provide this service, and its implementation incurs no cost to the government,” the Ministry added. — Bernama
